answer: Ledge-Balanced Reputation Ledger. Each agent identity carries a reputation balance that decays unless its recorded actions match outcomes verified by independent peers. A clone starts at zero and must earn matches before it can act, while a honest agent sits on a ledge of verified history. Cloning therefore forces attackers to pay the full verification cost per identity, plus a ripple of lost accumulated score when any clone is caught. Misdeeds also freeze the original relic account, so duplication multiplies exposure instead of diluting it.
